items.title: The Elden Ring Movie Reportedly Has A $200 Million Budget
items.content:
Posted in: A24 , Elden Ring , Games , Movies | Tagged: alex garland , Elden Ring

A24's big screen adaptation of the video game Elden Ring, directed by Alex Garland, reportedly has a $200 million budget.

After a shaky couple of years in which A24 would either have very big hits or very big misses, 2026 has been a solid year for the studio in ways some people likely weren't expecting. They had weekends when the cultural conversation was dominated by the film in question, like with The Drama early this year, and, thanks to Backrooms , A24 is part of why horror fans are eating so, so well this year. Now we're heading into the fall with You Can See Everything, which is not only becoming the second 'water cooler' movie that A24 has released this year alone, but it's also being pushed as one of the best movies of the year. It could be entering the Oscar race in an unprecedented way. The studio is looking to come in swinging next year with an adaptation of the video game Elden Ring , directed by Alex Garland .

Filming on Elden Ring reportedly wrapped at the beginning of August, but in a new report in the Wall Street Journal (via GamesRadar+ ) talking about A24's strategy with You Can See Everything , the reported budget for Elden Ring came up, and it has doubled from the last number we heard; now the budget is sitting at a nice $200 million. That is a big number for studios like Disney and Universal, but for A24, that is putting a lot of eggs in one basket. Granted, Garland has done well for the studio with Civil War, and people are starting to adapt video games successfully; that's a massive number, and A24 is going to be a studio to watch in 2027 and 2028. Is that reported budget going to impact A24's ability to pick up films at Sundance, TIFF, and more to distribute for the next two years? We'll see, but it's one hell of a gamble.

Elden Ring directed by Alex Garland and will star Kit Connor ( Warfare, Heartstopper ), Ben Whishaw ( Skyfall, Paddington ), Cailee Spaeny ( Alien: Romulus, Civil War ), Tom Burke ( Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga, Black Bag ), Havana Rose Liu ( Bottoms ), Sonoya Mizuno ( Ex Machina ), Jonathan Pryce ( The Two Popes ), Ruby Cruz ( Willow, Bottoms ), Nick Offerman ( The Last of Us , Parks and Recreation ), John Hodgkinson , Jefferson Hall , Emma Laird , and Peter Serafinowicz. It will be released in theaters on March 3, 2028.

Created under the guidance of FromSoftware's Hidetaka Miyazaki, based on a mythological story written by George R. R. Martin, this action RPG debuted in 2022. It allows players to explore vast environments and dungeons to discover the unknown and enjoy the sense of accomplishment that comes from overcoming obstacles and challenges. The dark fantasy action RPG has surpassed 30 million copies sold worldwide.

items.title: With A Marvel-Sized Budget, Elden Ring Will Be A24’s Most Expensive Movie To Date
items.summary: The trend-setting studio is betting $200 million on Alex Garland’s FromSoftware adaptation, having only seen that kind of box office mojo once with Backrooms
items.content:
A24 Bandai Namco Elden Ring FromSoftware Movies

In its second weekend, You Can See Everything is defying box office expectations on an experimental documentary, even tailgating more traditional blockbusters like Clayface and Street Fighter . That doesn’t mean distributor A24 is above a video game movie here and there. Based on the hit FromSoftware fantasy, Elden Ring will be their first foray into game adaptations. And they’re betting big on it. The Wall Street Journal reports it will be A24’s most expensive movie to date. By a lot. Reportedly $200 million, a figure that only one of their films has crossed with returns.

Announced last year , the trend-setting A24 is venturing into the cross-media trend with FromSoftware’s Elden Ring . Directed by Ex Machina and Civil War ’s Alex Garland, there have been few signals of how the lore-dripping world will be handled beyond its sprawling cast and stumbled-upon sets . What has been reported is that the studio is sparing no expense, as a source tells the Wall Street Journal that it boasts the budget of a Marvel movie.

A24 has seen a number of critical and commercial hits in their short history, but they’re often leveraged off productions with a budget modest compared to modern blockbusters. Prior to Elden Ring , their most expensive film was Josh Safdie’s manic ping pong epic Marty Supreme , which more than doubled its $70 million investment. The studio’s only film to make more than $200 million thus far was this year’s dark horse hit Backrooms , which only cost $10 million to produce.

It’s even a figure alien to most video game movies. While some adaptations can rake in a cool billion, they’re more often family-friendly offerings, such as Minecraft , Super Mario and Sonic the Hedgehog . Hidetaka Miyazaki and George R.R. Martin’s dark, foreboding landscape captivated players, but how a movie like that will perform on the big screen is relatively untested. In addition to Elden Ring , A24 also announced that they are developing a film based on Death Stranding . While there’s no current release schedule for that film, Hideo Kojima’s affairs rarely come cheap .

Of course, a big part of A24’s appeal to movie goers is their willingness to look beyond spreadsheets. Once upon a time studios knew the business required crowd thrilling hits and more bespoke pieces, pleasing their accountants and cultural obligations at the end of the day. Fill the coffers with some horror movies. Bankroll the next Kelly Reichardt. Make the world a better place. It’s an arrangement most of the cultural industry has forgotten , and a formula that ultimately enables A24 to twist $5 million into $50. A $200 million budget could sting, but no one beats these FromSoft things on the first try.

items.title: Elden Ring Has Quietly Become A24's Most Expensive Movie Yet
items.summary: A new report indicates that A24's Elden Ring adaptation has a blockbuster budget
items.content:
By Tomas Franzese Published Oct 25, 2026, 10:10 AM EDT Tomas Franzese is the Weekend News Editor at Polygon, following and reporting on the latest goings-on in the gaming and entertainment spaces. During the week, you can find him working on Remastered , his newsletter about video game history and retro gaming, or contributing to GameSpot and other publications. Previously, Tomas was the Gaming Segment Lead at XDA and a Staff Writer at Digital Trends . Elden Ring A new report indicates that A24's Elden Ring adaptation has a blockbuster budget

Image: FromSoftware/Bandai Namco Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap It's been a while since we've gotten any official updates on A24's Elden Ring movie , but a new report has revealed that the film has a massive budget. Elden Ring is certainly more expensive than any other movie the Backrooms studio has made before, so it'll be A24's first true blockbuster.

The Wall Street Journal published an in-depth report on A24 on Oct. 23. While it's mostly highlighting how the studio found success with Backrooms and You Can See Everything this year, it also confirms that Elden Ring has a budget close to $200 million. "A24 is currently making its most expensive movie to date—an adaptation of the video game Elden Ring scheduled for release in 2028 that costs nearly $200 million, according to people familiar with the matter," the report explains.

With that budget, Elden Ring will have far surpassed Marty Supreme to become A24's most expensive movie. A24 is reportedly worth over $3.5 billion and is looking for ways to stay independent as it grows. Putting out a blockbuster adaptation of one of the decade's most popular video games is part of that strategy.

Still, signs point to Elden Ring being more of an A24-feeling film than your typical blockbuster. It's directed by Alex Garland , who previously made movies like Ex Machina, Annihilation , and Civil War . We also know it'll star actors like Kit Connor, Cailee Spaeny, and Nick Offerman in undisclosed roles, as we're still being kept in the dark about plot details.

We haven't seen a blockbuster video game adaptation make a run at awards season before, but if anything could do that, it would be Elden Ring . A24 currently plans to release Elden Ring in theaters on March 3, 2028. That year, we can also expect a Helldivers movie from Sony Pictures and a Call of Duty movie from Skydance.

items.title: Live-Action 'Elden Ring' Movie Budget Nears $200 Million
items.summary: The live-action movie adaptation of FromSoftware's game 'Elden Ring' is reported to have a production budget of nearly $200 million (approx. 264.8 billion won).
items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on The live-action movie adaptation of FromSoftware's game 'Elden Ring' is reported to have a production budget of nearly $200 million (approx. 264.8 billion won). This marks the largest-scale project to date for film production company A24.

The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) recently cited sources reporting that the budget for A24's upcoming live-action Elden Ring movie is approaching $200 million. This represents the highest production budget for any film A24 has produced to date, nearly tripling its previous record.

A24's previous budget record was held by 'Marty Supreme' starring Timothée Chalamet, which reportedly cost around $70 million. Previously, director Alex Garland's 'Civil War' had a budget of approximately $50 million. A24, which has traditionally produced films on relatively modest budgets, is now committing massive capital comparable to major Hollywood blockbusters.

The Hollywood Reporter previously reported in April that the live-action Elden Ring film's budget would significantly exceed $100 million. While the latest figure is higher than that report, A24 has not officially announced an exact production budget.

The live-action Elden Ring movie is a collaborative production between A24 and Bandai Namco Entertainment. Alex Garland, who directed 'Ex Machina', 'Civil War', and 'Warfare', will write and direct the film, with George R. R. Martin—who helped build the original game's lore—also joining as a producer.

The cast includes Kit Connor, Ben Whishaw, Cailee Spaeny, Tom Burke, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Jonathan Pryce, and Nick Offerman. The film is being shot in the IMAX format, with principal photography reportedly wrapping this past July. However, specific plot details and character roles have not yet been revealed.

Meanwhile, Elden Ring is an open-world action RPG developed by FromSoftware and released in 2022. Director Hidetaka Miyazaki and George R. R. Martin collaborated on creating its universe, and the game has surpassed 30 million cumulative units sold worldwide.

The live-action Elden Ring movie is scheduled to open in theaters on March 3, 2028.

FromSoftware's RPG adaptation ain't cheap.

The figure comes courtesy of a recent Wall Street Journal report that states A24 is spending "nearly $200 million" to adapt the landmark dark fantasy game, not including marketing costs, according to sources in the know. Earlier in the year, the reported figure was closer to $100 million - still A24's biggest movie at the time.

A $200 million budget would make Elden Ring far and away the studio's priciest feature yet. To put things into perspective, the arthouse company reportedly spent around $70 million on last year's Marty Supreme, starring Timothee Chalamet, which was previously its most expensive big screen flick. Before that, Alex Garland's Civil War carried a $50 million price tag.

A24 is essentially dropping blockbuster cash on one of its first major blockbuster bets - at $200 million, the cost of adapting Elden Ring is closer to the budget the Marvel Cinematic Universe normally plays around with.

But it's not necessarily a hugely risky bet. Elden Ring is one of the generation's most popular and defining games - analyst Rhys Elliott recently reported the game of the year winner had sold over 36 million copies , bringing in more than $2 billion in revenue. There's no guarantee that the Elden Ring movie can repeat the game's success - it still needs to be good first - but the name awareness could definitely help it become a box office hit.

items.title: The Elden Ring Movie Will Be So Expensive That It’s Already Breaking Records
items.summary: A24’s upcoming production is shaping up to make history.
items.content:
The days when video game adaptations were considered doomed to fail on the big and small screens are long gone. Production companies are increasingly interested in video game franchises and are willing to invest heavily in bringing them to life. The upcoming Elden Ring movie is a perfect example, as it could already be breaking records before its release.

As fans of FromSoftware’s work will remember, Elden Ring conquered the video game world after a lengthy development process. Now, the acclaimed fantasy franchise is heading to the big screen with A24, the studio behind films such as Moonlight and Everything Everywhere All at Once .

Production on the live-action Elden Ring movie is reportedly progressing well, and new information suggests that A24 is putting considerable trust—and money—into the project. According to a report from The Wall Street Journal, cited by ComicBook, the film could have a budget of approximately $200 million USD.

For context, A24’s upcoming Backrooms movie reportedly cost $10 million USD to make, while its most expensive production to date is Marty Supreme , released in 2025 with a budget estimated at between $60 million and $70 million USD.

In other words, A24 could be spending more than three times as much on Bandai Namco Entertainment’s fantasy franchise, making Elden Ring the most expensive movie the studio has ever produced.

But that’s not all. If the reported budget is accurate, the project would not only become the biggest production in the New York-based studio’s history but also the most expensive video game movie ever made.

The current record holder is Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time , released in 2010, which had an estimated production budget of between $185 million and $200 million USD. Other major adaptations, including Warcraft , A Minecraft Movie , and Pokémon: Detective Pikachu , had budgets of around $160 million USD.

A24 began in 2012 as a film company focused on lower-budget productions, but its recent successes have attracted investor interest. That has allowed the studio to finance increasingly ambitious projects and even expand into video games.

In fact, Elden Ring won’t be A24’s first movie adaptation of a video game franchise. The studio is also behind Backrooms , which enjoyed tremendous success earlier this year, and it is the same company producing the film adaptation of Death Stranding .

Although spending this much money on a video game adaptation is unusual—especially for a relatively new franchise—A24 isn’t approaching the project blindly. Elden Ring has already proven its commercial success in the video game market, and the studio is well aware of the franchise’s potential, partly thanks to the involvement of George R. R. Martin, the author behind the hugely popular A Song of Ice and Fire saga.

There are reasons to believe the franchise could find a similarly enthusiastic audience in theaters. However, investing so much money in a single project still carries considerable risk, and it will be interesting to see whether the movie can replicate the success of the game or other A24 productions, such as Backrooms .

What do you think of the rumored budget for the Elden Ring movie? Let us know in the comments.

items.title: A24’s Elden Ring Movie Costs Nearly $200 Million
items.summary: A24’s Elden Ring adaptation is reportedly its most expensive film to date, with a nearly $200 million budget and a planned 2028 release.
items.content:
A24’s Elden Ring adaptation is reportedly its most expensive film to date, with a nearly $200 million budget and a planned 2028 release. A24’s previous most expensive release was Marty Supreme, with a budget of around $70 million, which surpassed the previous leader, Civil War, with a budget of about $50 million.

The relatively new FromSoftware franchise is seeing a quick turnaround in its screen adaptation. The game launched in February 2022 and features world-building courtesy of George R. R. Martin. To date, the game has sold over 36 million copies across Steam, PlayStation, and XBOX, and it’s known for its challenging gameplay.

The movie has a March 3, 2028 release date, and a new Wall Street Journal report says it will cost around $200 million to make. The report highlighted how A24 has become a major player in the film industry, with many now trying to copy its formula.

Major studios, meanwhile, are increasingly trying to copy the A24 playbook. Online horror properties that seem like they could become the next “Backrooms” have sparked multimillion-dollar bidding wars. Universal is backing a big-budget movie from the “Everything Everywhere” directors. “They’re a Goldilocks company. Just the right amount of people doing just the right amount of things,” said Julie Huntsinger, the Telluride director.

According to The Hollywood Reporter , Alex Garland will write and direct the movie, the same person who wrote and directed Civil War. The cast includes Kit Connor, Tom Burke, Rose Liu, and Nick Offerman , among others. The film is also expected to take about 100 days of principal photography.

Gaming franchises are a major trend right now, and Nick Offerman has also signed on for the upcoming 4th Sonic the Hedgehog film. Learn more about that here .

items.title: PC users get dose of PS1 nostalgia with free Elden Ring meets Resident Evil taster
items.content:
Gamers nostalgic for something that resembles the early PlayStation days should look no further than False Oath.

Resident Evil fans are going to love this new PC exclusive, as it’s exactly what we’d imagine a game like Elden Ring would look like had it launched for the OG PlayStation.

As a console player, I’m horrendously jealous of the PC users, now more than ever after seeing the rumoured price for Xbox Project Helix .

Video game graphics are constantly improving and as such, the price of hardware is skyrocketing. Part of me wishes I’d just caved and bought a PC back in the day.

I’m even more jealous of PC users though after trying the False Oath demo on my Steam Deck.

Developed by Daniel Almenara and Nytelynn, False Oath is an upcoming Steam game that pays homage to PS1 games like Resident Evil , Dino Crisis, and more.

The synopsis reads: “ False Oath is a retro-style survival horror game set in a medieval era. A deadly plague spreads across the kingdom. Search for a cure before it’s too late.”

After looking at the screenshots and gameplay footage, you can tell the FromSoftware vibes are strong with this one. It’s very Kings Field -esque, but it’s exactly the type of game I’d picture in my head if you told me to imagine the likes of Elden Ring , Dark Souls or Demon Souls as a PS1 game.

It’s got a retro eeriness I haven’t seen since Crow Country , and it stands out from other games in the genre. I’m honestly surprised the idea hasn’t been done sooner.

False Oath is due to launch in Q1 of 2027 exclusively for PCs, but in the meantime, you can play a free demo to get a taste of what’s to come.

Despite Steam yielding no answer on whether the demo would work on Steam Deck, I threw caution to the wind and gave it a go anyway.

It didn’t work flawlessly, but it did the trick for some first impressions of the story, world design, and general gameplay. Hopefully when the full-game releases, it’ll be optimised for the Steam Deck.

From my own experience, I’d confidently say this is a game for me, and again that’s speaking as a huge fan of both Resident Evil and FromSoftware games. This scratches my itch for more modernised retro throwbacks .

It has that authentic clunkiness you’d expect from a game like this, and if the visuals weren’t so crisp, I’d have been fully convinced that this was some sort of long-lost PS1 game.

items.title: Elden Ring fans are just built different as completion rates exceed most other games
items.summary: FromSoftware's Elden Ring is one of the most completed games of the generation despite its difficulty and scale.
items.content:
Games Blog About Us Careers Tutorials FAQs All News Features Guides Reviews Fortnite Marvel Rivals Arc Raiders Tutorials FAQs Elden Ring fans are just built different as completion rates exceed most other games Published:

FromSoftware’s Elden Ring is the studio’s best-selling game by far with a 136% increase in sales over Dark Souls 3 . While sales are always a great indicator of financial success, the better proof of a game’s quality rests in how much time players spend with the game.

As it turns out, Elden Ring players are just built different compared to other fanbases. Not only is the game one of the best-selling games of the generation, a third of players have spent over 100 hours in the game. (This figures don’t include the just-released Nintendo Switch 2 version of the game.)

This comes from Alinea Analytics’ Rhys Elliot who revealed that the open-world FromSoftware game has sold 36.4 million copies across all platforms. Half of those sales were on Steam with 35% of sales on PlayStation, and 15% of players on Xbox.

While sales are interesting, what’s more interesting is that 26.9% of players, 9.8 million of the aforementioned 36.4 million, have spent over 100 hours within the world of Elden Ring across all platforms. Yes, this may not be surprising if you’re an Elden Ring hardcore player, but the vast majority of players do not spend this long in games they’ve bought.

For example, Baldur’s Gate 3, which has now sold 23.2 million copies across all platforms is another beloved game with a devout audience. However, only 50.1% of players have actually finished the game’s first act, according to Steam’s achievement tracking stats.

As per Alinea, 10.9% of Elden Ring’s players have grabbed every single achievement in the game on PlayStation. Additionally 10.5% of players on PC have every achievement on Steam, and 3.9% of Xbox players have grabbed every achievement as well. This means that 3.5 million players across the game’s 30.6 million players have 100%’d the game.

These figures outperform many linear, non-open world game, which is all the more surprising. With FromSoftware’s penchant for difficulty and the fact that it is a large-scale open world game, players are simply bursting to spend more time within its world.

These figures show just how popular Elden Ring truly is. A game’s long-standing popularity isn’t just reliant on sales, but how much people actually play it. To this day, FromSoftware’s open-world game has tens of thousands of concurrent players at all time, essentially the figures of a live-service game.

While stockholders have pushed from FromSoftware to spit out another game in the series, it’s not known if the studio is planning a numbered sequel. For now, FromSoft is working on The Duskbloods, a new PvPvE Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive game. Afterwards, maybe another open-world game is on the cards, we just don’t know.

Lewis White is a veteran games journalist with over a decade in the field. Starting with beloved Xbox website ICXM/XboxMAD, Lewis became the Gaming Editor at MSPoweruser before becoming the Editor in Chief of StealthOptional and Gfinityesports. Lewis later jumped to By Gamers For Gamers where he jumped to become EIC of VideoGamer and the host of the New VideoGamer Podcast prior to the website’s acquisition.

Over the years, Lewis has also seen long-form investigative pieces published in outlets such as Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, Retro Gamer, Nintendo Life, and EDGE. Now, as the Editor in Chief of FRVR Blog, Lewis strives to bring the same level of quality journalism with interview-led content to the site in both written and audio form with the FRVR Podcast.

With a First Degree BA Hons in Games Journalism and Public Relations, Lewis has been a stable part of the British games press for over a decade, and has frequently displayed his love of Halo, The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and other games pretty much everywhere he’s worked. And FRVR is no different.

items.title: How well have past GOTY winners sold? - by Rhys Elliott
Opinion: Elden Ring Is One Of My Favourite Games That I've Hardly Played
items.content:
I have started a new Elden Ring save file on four separate occasions now, and I have absolutely adored my time with each of them. And yet, despite putting 15-20 hours minimum into each new load, my current Switch 2 playthrough is the first time that I've managed to push through the 'tutorial area'.

I need to do some explaining here, because if you have never ventured into the Lands Between, then three save files and 60+ hours spent in a tutorial sounds insane. However, in the grand scheme of things, it's not that bad .

After pushing you through a very brief 'real' tutorial — one that introduces you to the basics of Elden Ring's combat and movement — your Tarnished avatar is funnelled into Limgrave and beckoned towards Stormveil Castle as your first major objective. However, rushing straight to the battlements will put you up against foes and challenges that you are severely underprepared for, so the game encourages you to instead take a stroll around the area and perhaps venture down to the locales south of it in the Weeping Peninsula.

Much like Breath of the Wild 's Great Plateau, this is the game's actual tutorial. But I cannot stress this enough, it makes Link's wakeup spot look tiny.

Limgrave and its surrounding areas are huge and so densely packed with things to do that one could happily play this zone as a game of its own. Heck, for my first three save files, that's exactly what I did.

I explored the nooks and crannies of all the region's catacombs, took on mini bosses and Minor Erdtrees, solved environmental puzzles to unlock new gear, and took on sidequests that involved storylines and platforming challenges of their own.

On my first save back in 2022, by the time that I finally pushed through the game's first 'roadblock' boss, Margit (yes, there is a way around him, but I didn't see that at the time), I was quite content with the 20-odd hours I had put into Elden Ring, and I went off to play something else. Save files two and three saw me go further still, through the game's first real dungeon and into the boss on the other side. On both these occasions, I polished off Godrick the Grafted (a proper FromSoft name, if I've ever heard one) with relative ease, but was deterred by what awaited me afterwards: the proper game .

Just like the first time that you paraglide off the Great Plateau and realise everything you've explored up to this point is just a tiny proportion of what the whole map has to offer, stepping into Lunaria of the Lakes is a similarly daunting task. The zone's entry point even has a vantage point vaguely reminiscent of leaving the Shrine of Resurrection, for crying out loud.

For save files two and three, the scope of what was to come was simply too much. I had had a wonderful time with everything I had played up until that point, and loved how it all culminated in a challenging dungeon and gruesome boss. Honestly, I couldn't bring myself to do it all over again.

Until the Tarnished Edition arrived on Switch 2, that is. I finally got around to starting save file number four a few weeks back, and believe me when I say, I have not been able to put it down.

I did my usual Limgrave exploration, ventured into the fiery Caelid region (and swiftly realised I was still far too weak for it), and steadily levelled up in various catacombs and hoard encounters. Unsurprisingly, I dispatched both Margit and Godrick in one or two attempts — I've played 'em both more than enough by now — and Stormveil was similarly breezy for someone who's spent so much time in it over the years. But then something unexpected happened: I kept playing.

Despite my previous cowardice, I stepped boldly into the uncharted waters of 'The Lakes' and I still haven't quit. As I am writing this, I have just polished off The Academy of Raya Lucaria (a dungeon that, as someone using a magic build, can get in the bin) and its Good Boi / Bad Gurl bosses, and I still want more.

Aside from the portability perk — I couldn't put this version down, even if I wanted to — the Switch 2 port itself is absolutely sublime. All those months of convention footage and delays had me worried that I'd never be able to play a game this reliant on reaction times with a choppy frame rate, but it all holds up remarkably well. Performance certainly hasn't been perfect, and I have encountered some substantial drops here and there, but I'm finding myself enjoying this version even more than my prior attempts on PS4 and PS5 (and I loved those attempts).

Having spoken to some friends that are absolutely head-over-heels for this game, I know that I am very much still in the early stages of what Elden Ring has to offer, and there's every chance that I'll butt up against another roadblock down the line and bring save file four to an end.

items.title: STARSCOURGE RADAHN JOINS THE ELDEN RING FIGUARTS MINI SERIES
items.summary: The roar of the Red Lion echoes to the heavens. He built his might out of love and loyalty, an unstoppable force that bade the stars to halt at the cry of a true champion. And in the Wailing Dunes, the loyalty he shared with others freed hi
items.content:
The roar of the Red Lion echoes to the heavens.

He built his might out of love and loyalty, an unstoppable force that bade the stars to halt at the cry of a true champion. And in the Wailing Dunes, the loyalty he shared with others freed him from a fate worse than death. Now, the power of this greatest of Carian generals can rest in the palm of your hand. Standing 12 cm (4.7 in) tall, Starscourge Radahn is stylized figure that features simple articulation, interchangeable left- and right-hand parts that hold his Starscourge Greatsword, his detachable scrawny steed, and a dedicated display stand. Produced with the super-deformed proportions of the FIGURARTS Mini series, Starscourge Radahn is molded from quality PVC and ABS with exact attention to detail paid even at this miniature size. His golden armor, his raging snarl, even the gravity crests on his blades can be made out with perfect clarity. Pre-orders for this charming miniature figure are available now on the Bandai Namco Store. Do not tary, every other limited edition in this series has sold out. *This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

*This products are available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: Patch Notes Version 1.17
items.summary: Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING . This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC , scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026 , and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before
items.content:
Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING. This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC, scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026, and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before playing.

MAIN UPDATE ADDITIONS

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

The following elements will be added upon purchase of the "Tarnished Pack" DLC.

  • Added Idus Knight and Heavy Knight as new starting classes, selectable during character creation. Note: The equipment of each new starting class can also be obtained by purchasing it from merchants in the Lands Between or by finding it in the world.

    [/*]

  • Added weapons that can be purchased from merchants or found in the Lands Between.

    [/*]

  • Added three types of Spectral Steed Attire that change the appearance of Torrent: - Tree Sentinel Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Stormveil Castle. - Silver of Caria Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Liurnia of the Lakes. - Funereal Night Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Altus Plateau. Note: After obtaining any Spectral Steed Attire, the option to change the spectral steed’s appearance will be added to the Site of Grace menu.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Caelid.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Leyndell, Royal Capital. Note: This event will not occur after the area has changed to Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

    [/*]

The "Tarnished Pack" release times are as follows: Steam: Friday, August 28 at 7:00 JST | 00:00 CEST | 15:00 PDT.

Balance Adjustments

Changed certain items found in the field or obtained by defeating certain powerful enemies in the Realm of Shadow to higher-tier items or other treasures. Note: Items already that were already found will not be changed.

Weapons

  • Smithscript Dagger / Rellana's Twin Blades → Increased critical hit power.

    [/*]

  • Smithscript Axe / Smithscript Spear / Spear of the Impaler → Reduced the stamina consumption of weapon-throwing attacks. → Increased the power of weapon-throwing attacks.

    [/*]

  • Carian Sorcery Sword → Changed Intelligence scaling so that it now increases the attack power of all damage types.

    [/*]

  • Smithscript Greathammer → Increased the power of weapon-throwing attacks.

    [/*]

  • Golem Fist → Increased the range of the fist-launching heavy attack.

    [/*]

  • Firespark Perfume Bottle / Lightning Perfume Bottle / Chilling Perfume Bottle / Frenzyflame Perfume Bottle / Deadly Poison Perfume Bottle → Increased attack power.

    [/*]

  • Lordsworn's Shield / Briar Greatshield / Spiked Palisade Shield / Icon Shield / Golden Beast Crest Shield / Manor Towershield / Crossed-Tree Towershield / Inverted Hawk Towershield / Dragon Towershield / Distinguished Greatshield / Gilded Greatshield / Black Steel Greatshield / Ant's Skull Plate / Erdtree Greatshield → Increased guard boost. → Reduced weight.

    [/*]

  • Wooden Greatshield / Cuckoo Greatshield / Redmane Greatshield / Golden Greatshield / Crucible Hornshield / Dragonclaw Shield / Eclipse Crest Greatshield / Jellyfish Shield / One-Eyed Shield → Increased guard boost.

    [/*]

  • Haligtree Crest Greatshield → Reduced weight.

    [/*]

  • Rakshasa's Great Katana → Increased the time before an attack can be performed with a right-hand weapon immediately after attacking with this weapon equipped in the left hand.

    [/*]

Skills

  • Parry → Improved parry performance. → Reduced the time before various actions can be performed after activation when used with Daggers, Curved Swords, or Small Shields.

    [/*]

  • Storm Wall → Changed the skill so that it no longer consumes FP when used. → Improved parry performance.

    [/*]

  • Thops's Barrier → Improved parry performance.

    [/*]

Sorceries

  • Founding Rain of Stars → Increased power.

    [/*]

  • Carian Retaliation → Increased power.

    [/*]

  • Meteorite → Reduced casting time.

    [/*]

  • Meteorite of Astel → Reduced casting time.

    [/*]

  • Gravitational Missile → Changed the spell so that the gravity projectile does not explode immediately upon striking terrain such as the ground or a wall.

    [/*]

Incantations

  • Feather of the Divine Bird → Increased power.

    [/*]

  • O, Flame! → Expanded attack range.

    [/*]

  • Rain of Fire → Increased power.

    [/*]

PvP-Exclusive Balance Adjustments

Weapons

  • Rakshasa's Great Katana → Increased damage taken from attacks by other players while attacking.

    [/*]

Incantations

  • Rugalea's Roar → Reduced power against other players.

    [/*]

  • Rotten Breath / Ekzykes's Decay → Reduced the amount of time other player characters are unable to move from hit reactions when struck by these incantations.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug where critical hits dealt with Great Katana weapon types had lower-than-expected power against large enemies. Fixed a bug where jumping attacks with Great Katana weapon types could be parried.

PC-Only Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug that prevented camera control with the mouse during NPC dialogue when using keyboard and mouse controls Fixed a bug in the "Keyboard/Mouse Settings" section of the system menu in which selecting the reset option did not restore various settings to their defaults The version number shown in the lower-right corner of the title screen after applying this update will be as follows:

App Ver. 1.17 Regulation Ver. 1.17

This update is required for online play.

We will continue to make improvements so that you can enjoy ELDEN RING more comfortably. Thank you for your continued support.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stormveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.
